limits: The map fixes city geography; generated lots do not identify individual 1871 buildings or addresses.
The 1869 municipal outline bounds context; Mitchell's 1870 sheet does not cover every western and southern annexation, so peripheral street and settlement patterns are reconstructed.
Generic period building forms, textures, vegetation and center-pivot bridge details are bounded reconstructions, not photographic matches.
City population, households and building totals are separate historical quantities; the contextual instance count is not a census count.

unbuilt_ground.name: Lake Park, Michigan Avenue to the breakwater
unbuilt_ground.note: Mitchell's 1870 map prints LAKE PARK on the strip east of Michigan Avenue from Randolph Street to Park Place (by Twelfth Street), with the Illinois Central breakwater and trestle beyond it. No generic building is placed there; the depot ground north of Randolph and the built avenues south of Twelfth keep theirs.

bridges.name: State Street bridge
bridges.approach: The deck runs from the drawn street's end on one bank to its end on the other (T-3751), so the street is carried over the river in its own line and width; the swing span is the reported length, centred on its pivot where the deck crosses the river line.
bridges.form: centre-pivot swing span on a round stone pivot pier inside a timber protection pier: a timber deck with railed footways, two timber trusses deepest over the pivot with a central tower and iron tie rods to the ends; fixed timber approach spans on pile bents carry the deck to the street on both banks

street_names.note: T-3684. Inside the core polygon every street is a platted line named from 1870-71 sources (name_basis on each segment: edwards_1871, mitchell_1870, plat; unread = drawn on the 1870 map, name not legible, name null). Outside it the mapped arterials run on splines through their traced points; the lattice (name null, name_basis reconstructed) fills whole blocks between them.
